title: Integer-shift compatibility of the normalized slice tensor comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the universe of module sheaves, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings and $W\in\mathcal C$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the localized ringed site $(\mathcal C/W,\mathcal O_W)$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and exact derived restriction $r:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O_W)$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]; also write $r$ for termwise restriction of complexes. Write $T(A,B)=\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_{\mathcal O}B)$ and $T_W$ for its slice version, with differential $d_A\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_B$ on bidegree $(p,q)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Use K-flat complexes with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution] and their integer-shift stability [lem-sfb-kflat-homotopy-triangulated]; the shift has $(A[n])^p=A^{p+n}$ and differential $(-1)^nd_A$. Let $\rho_{M,N}:r(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}N)\xrightarrow{\sim}rM\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_W}rN$ be the canonical comparison with precisely the tensor-model normalization in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose]: for flat-term K-flat $A,B$ representing $M,N$, $rA,rB$ are flat-term K-flat and $\rho$ is represented, through the canonical tensor-model isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], by $m_{A,B}:rT(A,B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W(rA,rB)$, whose $(p,q)$ summand is $\mu_{A^p,B^q}:(A^p\otimes B^q)|_W\cong A^p|_W\otimes B^q|_W$, sending local $x\otimes y$ to $x\otimes y$.
For every integer $n$, use the natural chain shift isomorphisms $s^1_n:T(A[n],B)\cong T(A,B)[n]$ and $s^2_n:T(A,B[n])\cong T(A,B)[n]$, unsigned in the first variable and with coefficient $(-1)^{np}$ on a summand of first degree $p$ in the second variable [lem-weil-pbc-total-tensor-integer-shifts], and their slice versions. With the termwise identification $r(A[n])=(rA)[n]$, the following are equalities of chain maps:
$$s^1_{W,n}\circ m_{A[n],B}=m_{A,B}[n]\circ r(s^1_n),\qquad s^2_{W,n}\circ m_{A,B[n]}=m_{A,B}[n]\circ r(s^2_n).$$
On bidegree $(p,q)$ both routes in the first equality are $\mu_{A^{p+n},B^q}$ with coefficient $1$; both routes in the second are $(-1)^{np}\mu_{A^p,B^{q+n}}$. These formulas hold for every flat-term K-flat pair and its shifted pairs. On arbitrary $M,N\in D(\mathcal O)$, put $\Phi(M,N)=r(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}N)$ and $\Psi(M,N)=rM\otimes^{\mathbf L}rN$. Give them the composite shift comparisons induced by the termwise restriction shifts and the localized $s^1,s^2$. For $Z_1=(M[n],N)$ and $Z_2=(M,N[n])$ one has, naturally in both inputs,
$$s^i_{\Psi,n}\circ\rho_{Z_i}=\rho_{M,N}[n]\circ s^i_{\Phi,n}\quad(i=1,2).$$
The equalities hold for any tensor presentations with the stated normalization, independently of the flat-term K-flat representatives, without boundedness or perfectness assumptions.

proof.text: The resolving class is closed under all the shifts in the statement, without a boundedness assumption. Indeed, if $A$ is K-flat and $E$ is acyclic, the second-variable chain isomorphism gives $T(E,A[n])\cong T(E,A)[n]$. The right side is acyclic by K-flatness of $A$: shifting just reindexes kernels and images, and multiplying a differential by $(-1)^n$ changes neither. Thus $A[n]$ is K-flat by definition. Its terms are flat because they are the terms $A^{p+n}$ of $A$. The identical argument applies to $B$ and over $\mathcal O_W$.

proof.text:
Choose flat-term K-flat resolutions $A,B$ of complexes representing $M,N$, using the resolution theorem. Use the canonical tensor-model isomorphisms of the descent theorem. The normalization of $\rho$ in the cited slice-comparison statement identifies it with the chain isomorphism $m_{A,B}$ and says that $rA,rB$ are flat-term K-flat. By Step 1 the same normalization applies to $(A[n],B)$ and $(A,B[n])$. Restriction is sectionwise restriction of module maps, so $r(A[n])=(rA)[n]$: both differentials are $(-1)^nr(d_A)$. The tensor restriction isomorphisms $\mu$ are natural in both sheaves. Explicitly, for maps $f:A\to A'$ and $g:B\to B'$ their summand identity is
$$\mu_{A'^p,B'^q}\,r(f^p\otimes g^q)=(rf^p\otimes rg^q)\,\mu_{A^p,B^q}.$$
Consequently the model comparisons are natural in both complex variables.

proof.text: For the first-variable square, fix total source degree $k$ and its summand indexed by $p+q=k$. The first-factor sheaf is $A^{p+n}$. The map $m_{A[n],B}$ has summand $\mu_{A^{p+n},B^q}$, and the following slice shift is unsigned. On the other route the restricted first-variable shift is unsigned, reindexes the first degree to $p+n$, and $m_{A,B}[n]$ again has summand $\mu_{A^{p+n},B^q}$. Both land in the summand indexed by $(p+n,q)$ of target degree $k+n$. Hence the two maps agree on every direct-sum constituent, so agree in degree $k$, and therefore as chain maps. Here the direct-sum identifications on the restricted side are exactly those in the specified model isomorphism $m$; no assertion about arbitrary infinite products is used.

source.place: Tag 0FNH, item-shift-tensor in section-sign-rules; agent-written calculation for the normalized slice map.

proof.text: For the second-variable square, a source summand in degree $k=p+q$ has sheaves $A^p,B^{q+n}$. Applying $m_{A,B[n]}$ and then $s^2_{W,n}$ gives $(-1)^{np}\mu_{A^p,B^{q+n}}$, landing in the target summand indexed by $(p,q+n)$. On the other route restriction of $s^2_n$ contributes the same $(-1)^{np}$, since restriction of module maps preserves their additive inverses; $m_{A,B}[n]$ then applies $\mu_{A^p,B^{q+n}}$. This is the same map because $\mu$ is a module morphism. Agreement on all direct-sum constituents proves equality in every degree and hence of chain maps. No additional sign comes from shifting a chain map: it is just reindexed. The argument uses parity of the integer $np$, so includes negative $n,p$.

proof.text:
Fix $n$. For $i=1,2$ let $F_1(M,N)=(M[n],N)$, $F_2(M,N)=(M,N[n])$, and let $S_n$ be shift on the target derived category. The derived tensor shift-descent theorem gives the natural shifts of the specified tensor bifunctors, with components computed by the localized $s^1_n,s^2_n$ on every resolving pair. Apply it over both $\mathcal O$ and $\mathcal O_W$; Step 1 supplies its shift-stability hypothesis in both places. Exact restriction is the functor of the derived-restriction definition. The exact-functor factorization theorem says its comparison between derived restriction and termwise restriction commutes with shifts. Thus, under the canonical tensor-model identifications of Step 2, the components on $(Q A,Q B)$ of the two natural transformations
$$L_i=s^i_{\Psi,n}\circ(\rho F_i),\qquad R_i=(S_n\rho)\circ s^i_{\Phi,n}:\Phi F_i\Longrightarrow S_n\Psi$$
are precisely the localizations of the two chain composites in Steps 3 and 4. All intervening factorization and tensor-model isomorphisms are the specified ones, and the intermediate inverse pairs cancel. Applying localization to those chain equalities therefore proves $L_i=R_i$ on every flat-term K-flat pair.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 06YU (definition-derived-tor and preceding construction), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); normalized models as stated in lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-evaluation-transpose.

proof.text: Apply the natural-transformation uniqueness clause of the tensor-descent theorem over $\mathcal O$, taking its target category $E=D(\mathcal O_W)$, its source bifunctor $U=\Phi F_i$ and its target bifunctor $V=S_n\Psi$. Its small-site hypothesis is exactly the hypothesis here. The restrictions of $L_i,R_i$ along $Q|_{\mathcal P}\times Q|_{\mathcal P}$ agree by Step 5; the uniqueness clause gives $L_i=R_i$ on $D(\mathcal O)\times D(\mathcal O)$. This proves the required identity naturally in both inputs. The tensor-model identifications are natural in homotopy-category maps and compatible with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms by that same cited statement. Consequently changing resolving representatives, or passing along any word of morphisms and inverted quasi-isomorphisms between them, leaves both transformations unchanged. Any other tensor presentation with the stipulated normalization has these same restricted components and hence these same transformations by uniqueness. Thus the equality holds independently of representatives and presentations for arbitrary unbounded objects.

The delivery splits the existing item into 6 steps, creates no new nodes and keeps the statement unchanged. proof_deps is exactly the union of the step uses, all cited ids exist and none is merged, and no cited node depends on the item, so there is no cycle. No SGA is used and there is no repair note for this item. Source: Stacks 0FNH (more-algebra.tex item-shift-tensor) puts the sign (-1)^{pb} on M^p⊗N^q, where p is the unshifted first degree. I recomputed the signs with the item's conventions: the first-variable shift needs no sign and the second needs (-1)^{np}, as the item says. Step 1 proves that flat-term K-flat complexes stay K-flat after a shift, using the second-variable shift isomorphism. That is the correct variable, because def-pc-kflat-complex puts the acyclic complex first. Steps 2-4 check the two chain squares summand by summand from the stated tensor-model normalization of ρ in the transpose node, using the naturality and sectionwise restriction stated in the cited nodes. Step 5 combines lem-weil-pbc-derived-tensor-shift-descent, which uses the same descent isomorphisms as ρ and gets its shift-stability hypothesis from Step 1, with clause (2) of the exact-functor factorization node. Step 6 applies the uniqueness clause for arbitrary transformations in lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent. Edge cases n=0, odd n and p, negative n, and unbounded complexes all check out. The blueprint place is the first paragraph of lemma-weil-pbc-perfect-projection-formula in main-20261015. Both declared tool_uses are accepted: the transpose node for its tensor-model normalization only, and the slice tensor-restriction node for naturality only. Advisory for the maintainer: lem-weil-pbc-pullback-tensor-canonical-shift-unit, created by NG the same day, gives the derived clause of this item after transport along the unit isomorphism. The parent's review already judged this not a duplicate, and I agree. Also, the statement cites the unsplit two-sided node lem-sfb-kflat-homotopy-triangulated for shift stability, but the proof does not rely on it.
